ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The control block diagram in the attached figure is, from left to right, input X, the first summing point, block G2, the second summing point, block G1, and the output is Y. The input on the left side of the first summing point is marked +, and the external feedback from output Y enters from below and is marked -. The signal from G2 on the left side of the second summing point is marked +, and output Y passes through H1 and then feeds back into the second summing point from below and is marked -. Reasoning: Let the output of the first summing point be e1; then from the signs in the figure, e1 = X - Y. After passing through G2, the signal is G2(X - Y). Let the output of the second summing point be e2; then e2 = G2(X - Y) - H1Y. The output satisfies Y = G1 e2, therefore Y = G1[G2(X - Y) - H1Y] = G1G2X - G1G2Y - G1H1Y. Transposing terms gives Y(1 + G1G2 + G1H1) = G1G2X, so the closed-loop gain G = Y/X = G1G2/(1 + G1G2 + G1H1).

raw_record.question_text: The block diagram of a feedback control system is shown in the image. What is the overall closed-loop gain \(G\) of the system?

method.method_draft: Let the first summing junction output be e1. From the image, e1 = X - Y because the outer feedback from Y is subtracted. After G2, the signal is G2(X - Y). Let the second summing junction output be e2. The image shows the G2 signal entering with plus sign and the H1 feedback from Y entering with minus sign, so e2 = G2(X - Y) - H1Y. The output is then Y = G1 e2. Substitute and rearrange: Y = G1[G2(X - Y) - H1Y] = G1G2X - G1G2Y - G1H1Y, so Y(1 + G1G2 + G1H1) = G1G2X. Therefore the overall closed-loop gain is G = Y/X = G1G2/(1 + G1G2 + G1H1).

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct signal-flow equation method: it uses the two visible summing junctions and feedback paths to write algebraic node equations, rather than trying to collapse blocks graphically first. This is the natural single-solution route for this diagram.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram structure: input X enters a first summing junction with a positive input from X and a negative unity feedback from the output Y; the result passes through block G2; then a second summing junction adds the G2 output positively and subtracts a feedback signal H1Y coming from the output through block H1; the result passes through block G1 to produce output Y.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to identify the requested quantity as the overall closed-loop gain G of the shown feedback control system, i.e. the ratio of output Y to input X.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard block-diagram rules: output of a summing junction is the signed sum of its inputs, output of a block equals its transfer function times its input, and closed-loop gain is Y/X. Solve the resulting linear algebraic equation for Y/X.
